properties.name: The design surfaces what was BUILT and is USED BY NOTHING — implemented effort that no longer earns its keep
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-09, promoting this from the vocabulary finding to a stated need: \"I know in the storyflow set of services, there are going to be multiple designed and implemented, but unused features. so having something in reflow2 that is able to automatically detect and surface these types 'implemented, but unused' aspects would be very beneficial.\"

THE NEED, and it is the mirror of everything reflow2 already computes. Every existing gap asks whether something is MISSING — nothing satisfies this requirement, nothing builds this capability, nothing verifies it. Not one asks whether something is SURPLUS: built, working, and consumed by nothing. On a long-lived system that is where the cost accumulates, because unused code is maintained, upgraded, secured and carried into every migration by people who cannot tell it is dead.

WHY NO EXISTING DETECTOR COVERS IT, checked against all seven capability gaps rather than assumed. `unallocated_capability` asks if it has a component. `unmotivated_capability` asks if it satisfies a requirement — INTENT, not use, and it is gated on requirements > 0. `unrealized_capability` asks if anything builds it. `unverified_capability` and `unvalidated_capability` ask about checks. NONE OF THEM ASKS WHETHER ANYTHING IS DOWNSTREAM OF IT.

THE COMPUTABLE FORM, and it is genuinely available today: a Capability at `realized`/`verified` that nothing DEPENDS_ON, that no Flow includes via PART_OF_FLOW, and that no Actor INTERACTS_WITH — built, and nothing in the design consumes it. The same shape reads for a Component (nothing CONSUMES its Interfaces) and for an Artifact (realizes nothing that anything needs).

⚠️ THE BOUND, WHICH MUST SHIP WITH IT AND NOT BE DISCOVERED LATER: THE GRAPH SEES DESIGN-LEVEL DEMAND, NEVER RUNTIME USAGE. A feature real users call every day, whose consumer was simply never modelled, is indistinguishable from a dead one. So this finding is \"NOTHING IN THE DESIGN CONSUMES THIS\", which is a statement about the design's completeness as much as about the system — and it must SAY that, or it becomes a tool that confidently recommends deleting working features. That is the same class as `unmet_needs: 0` reading as \"nothing is missing\" when it meant \"we never said we needed anything\".

TWO TIERS, and only the first is buildable now:
  (1) DESIGN-LEVEL — built, and nothing the design records consumes it. Computable from the graph as it stands.
  (2) RUNTIME-LEVEL — consumed in the design, but no real user ever calls it. Needs telemetry, and reflow2 already holds that question twice: dec:bl-155 (40 of 132 served tools never called, and reflow2 cannot tell unused from unreachable) and dec:idea-measure-the-surface (should real usage telemetry be a standing instrument, and how far may it go). Tier 2 belongs to those, not here.

PROVENANCE OF THE ASK: it arrived from the vocabulary sweep in dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches — eight declared edge types nothing reaches — but Anthony's need is the CONSUMER-FACING generalisation, and it is the larger of the two. This one is about somebody else's services, which is what rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party asks for.

RECORDED AT `proposed`: he stated a need clearly, and only his word moves a requirement off proposed.
